title: Status page automation ideas (scratchpad) — incident-bot prompts + autofill + false-positive risks
content:
Personal scratchpad. Not a spec. Capturing ideas + failure modes for automating public status updates (Statuspage) through incident-bot, without increasing on-call burden or publishing inaccurate/overconfident statements.

Context
- We keep getting the same pattern: incident starts, we know *something* is wrong, but we’re unsure which component(s)/region(s) are impacted. First update is slow, and/or we mark too broad (“API Degraded” everywhere).
- Goal for automation: reduce time-to-first-update (TTFU) and increase component accuracy, while avoiding noisy flips and false positives.
- Reminder: don’t over-promise on SLAs; don’t disclose customer-specific capacity/tenancy details; Dedicated/Private need careful language.

Working principles (guardrails)
1) Human remains accountable. Bot should draft + prefill, not “declare incidents” by itself (except maybe low-stakes advisory mode).
2) Automation must be reversible. Every automated action needs audit trail + idempotency key.
3) Default to conservative: better to say “Investigating elevated errors in US-East Streaming” than “Outage across Hosted API” unless verified.
4) Anti-flap is mandatory. Avoid toggling component status from transient spikes.
5) Keep the cognitive load low: one place to check (dashboard link), one place to approve, minimal free-text required for first update.

Idea bucket A — Autofill fields at incident intake (structured metadata)
- At incident creation / Sev escalation, require:
  - region (us-east, us-west, eu-west, ap-southeast, global/unknown)
  - product surface (Hosted API, Streaming, Embeddings, Reranking, Console)
  - capability (chat/generate vs embeddings vs rerank vs console)
  - confidence (low/medium/high) + evidence link (dashboard URL)
  - impact type (errors, latency, timeouts, disconnects)
- Autofill candidates based on:
  - alert labels (component_id / region / capability)
  - gateway metrics tags (route, model family, streaming=true)
  - incident channel name conventions (e.g., #inc-<date>-<region>-<surface>) — risky but helpful
  - last 15m top failing routes by error count (ranked list)

Notes
- Make “unknown” acceptable but visible: if region=unknown, bot should prompt “pick best guess or explicitly set unknown; update within 15m.”
- If multiple regions: allow multi-select but prompt to split into separate components where possible.

Idea bucket B — Draft status updates from incident state (templates + fill-ins)
Draft generator inputs
- incident state (Investigating / Identified / Mitigating / Monitoring / Resolved)
- affected components (structured list)
- what we see (errors %, p95 latency, disconnect rate) — ideally with a short plain-English description
- what customers might notice (timeouts, elevated errors, streaming disconnects)
- current mitigation / workaround (if safe to share)
- next update time

Draft generator outputs
- Title suggestion: "Degraded performance for Streaming in US-East" (avoid “outage” unless hard down)
- Message blocks that follow our tone guide:
  - Investigating: acknowledge + scoped symptoms, minimal speculation
  - Identified: describe contributing factor in non-sensitive terms (e.g., "increased error rates in gateway layer" vs "GPU pool exhausted for customer X")
  - Mitigating: actions taken (failover, rollback, scaling)
  - Monitoring: what metrics are improving, what’s left
  - Resolved: when impact ended, brief prevention steps, link to post-incident summary when available

Prompt text to force good behavior (bot asks the human)
- “Which component(s) should be marked? (Pick from registry)”
- “What evidence supports this selection? (dashboard link required for Sev0/Sev1)”
- “Is this impacting Dedicated/Private customers? If yes, do NOT name customers; use ‘Dedicated control plane’ component if applicable + coordinate with Support.”
- “Confirm next update time (default 30m for ongoing Sev1+, 60m for Sev2).”

Concerns
- Drafts can sound too confident. Add explicit uncertainty language for low confidence (“We are investigating reports of…”, “Some requests may…”).
- Avoid internal jargon: scheduler, KV cache, shard, etc.

Idea bucket C — Signal-driven suggestions (NOT full automation)
Suggestion mode (recommended)
- Bot posts in #incidents thread:
  - “Suggested impacted component(s): Streaming / US-East (confidence: medium) based on disconnect rate > threshold and p95 time-to-first-token > threshold.”
  - Provide a one-click button to apply on Statuspage (with human approval).

Full automation mode (maybe later, scary)
- Automatically set component to “Degraded Performance” if:
  - error burn rate breaches AND persists beyond anti-flap window
  - AND at least two independent signals agree (e.g., gateway errors + client disconnects)
  - AND a human has opened an incident or acknowledged alert

Anti-flap / false positive controls (must-have)
- Hysteresis: degrade threshold is stricter than recover threshold.
- Minimum duration: require 10–15m sustained breach before marking public degrade.
- Multi-window check: 5m + 30m windows to catch both spikes and sustained issues.
- “Manual override wins” with a cooling-off period (don’t immediately re-mark degraded if human just set operational).

Edge cases to explicitly handle
- Latency-only incidents: when do we publish? (Customers do care; but we need consistent criteria.)
  - Proposal: publish if p95 latency exceeds X for Y minutes AND error budget burn indicates meaningful impact.
- Partial routing impact: only a subset of models/routes failing.
  - Public component is coarse; message should mention “some requests” or “subset of routes” (avoid listing specific customer routes if sensitive).
- Capacity constraints / throttling: can look like errors.
  - Risk of revealing supply/capacity issues. Phrase as “elevated errors/timeouts” and avoid “out of capacity” language.

Idea bucket D — Approval workflow (lightweight)
- For Sev0/Sv1:
  - Add optional approval step before publishing update:
    - approver: IC or designated Comms Lead; Support lead approval if customer comms risk (Dedicated/Private visibility)
  - Timebox approvals (e.g., auto-expire in 5 min, falls back to IC) to avoid blocking urgent updates.
- For Sev2+:
  - Comms Lead can publish without additional approval.

Operational details
- Audit log should capture:
  - who approved
  - what changed (component, status, text diff)
  - when
  - associated incident id
- Statuspage API client needs retries/backoff + idempotency keys to prevent dupes.

Idea bucket E — Auto-generate post-incident summary (publishable)
- Generate a draft summary immediately at resolve time using:
  - incident timeline events (state changes, mitigation actions)
  - impact window (start/end)
  - affected components/regions
  - symptom metrics (peak error %, peak p95 latency)
  - root cause classification (dropdown taxonomy; free text optional)
- Then require human edit + quick legal/security pass only if it touches Dedicated/Private or anything potentially sensitive.

Confidentiality filters (draft tool should warn)
- Red flags in text: customer names, specific tenant ids, specific cluster names, exact capacity numbers (“we had N GPUs”), vendor incident details under NDA.
- Replace with safe phrasing suggestions.

Idea bucket F — Accuracy audits + feedback loop
- Weekly job compares:
  - incident tags (component/region) vs statuspage component updates
  - whether updates were timely (TTFU) and whether we over-scoped
- Output:
  - mismatch report by component
  - top 5 “misclassification patterns” (e.g., embeddings errors tagged as API)
  - recommended instrumentation changes

Failure modes / “how this goes wrong” list
1) False positive degrade => customer panic / trust hit.
2) Flapping statuses => looks chaotic, creates support load.
3) Under-scoping => customers experiencing impact but status shows green.
4) Over-scoping => implies global impact when only one region/capability.
5) Sensitive disclosure => “capacity exhausted” / mentions of specific customers.
6) Slowed comms due to too many required fields.

Mitigations
- Suggestion mode first (no automated publishing).
- Mandatory dashboard link for high severity.
- Anti-flap + confidence score displayed internally.
- Templates that are safe even when wrong (use cautious language).

Quick checklist for what to build first (MVP)
- [ ] Incident intake: add structured component/region/capability fields + validation
- [ ] Draft generator for Investigating + Identified (most time-critical)
- [ ] One-click “apply component selection to statuspage incident draft”
- [ ] Statuspage API client wrapper + audit log
- [ ] Add links to correct dashboards/runbooks per component

Open questions (bring to Rafael/Christine)
- What is the exact component registry source-of-truth? (repo vs Confluence; review process)
- Dedicated/Private: do we ever show regional components publicly, or only generic “Dedicated control plane signals”?
- Who is final approver for Sev0 wording if Legal/Security is asleep? (fallback rule)
- How do we avoid bot drafts becoming the de facto official comms without proper review?

Notes to self
- Watch out for “automation creep”: every optional feature adds new failure modes. Keep the initial flow dead simple.
- Biggest value is not fancy ML; it’s getting the right structured fields + safe templates + links that reduce writing time.
